oh-my-agent

 Ship 400+ commits a day.

 Install

 For humans

Run this from your project root.

 

 For AI agents

Paste this into your coding agent:

 

The agent installation guide covers non-interactive setup and verification. If you are the agent, read that guide and carry out the installation.

Then open your agent and type /orchestrate build a TODO app with login .

oh-my-agent ( oma ) turns Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and 11 other coding agents into a team. A planner splits the work, engineers build in parallel, a reviewer checks the result, and a debugger fixes the root cause.

 Start with your task

Pick a task. Load one skill into the agent you already use, or install the whole team.

 Your task Start here First request 
 --- --- --- 
 Review AI-written code bunx skills use first-fluke/oh-my-agent@oma-qa "Review this diff for bugs and missing checks. Cite the affected lines." 
 Design an admin screen bunx skills use first-fluke/oh-my-agent@oma-design "Review the hierarchy and table density of our admin page." 
 Fix a failing test bunx skills use first-fluke/oh-my-agent@oma-debug "Reproduce this test failure, fix its cause, and run the affected checks." 
 Review system boundaries bunx skills use first-fluke/oh-my-agent@oma-architecture "Review the boundary between our API and worker." 
 Run the whole team Install oma /orchestrate add login to this app 

Run the skills use command in your agent's terminal. It loads that one skill. For the full team with workflows, install oma. Other options are in Choose a setup.

 

After installing, run oma doctor . Your first 5 minutes starts with a read-only task before team workflows.

 What you get

 Workflows are what you type (or just say). They call in roles , the specialists. Skills are the know-how: each role carries its own, and your agent loads the rest whenever a task needs them.

 What it gives you Try it 
 --- --- --- 
 12 specialist roles PM, architect, backend, frontend, mobile, database and infra engineers, QA reviewer, debugger, refactorer, docs curator, researcher (meet them) /orchestrate build a TODO app with login 
 20 workflows Slash commands from /brainstorm and /plan to /review , /debug and /scm . The four multi-agent modes also start when a plain request names them "ultrawork: add rate limiting" 
 32 skills Domain know-how that loads only when a task needs it: UI, APIs, schemas, Terraform, CI, security, git, observability loads by itself, e.g. "add a Terraform S3 bucket" 
 Files you can open Plans, design docs, API contracts, ADRs, bug notes, per-agent results, security evidence, HTML explainers, recaps ls .agents/results 
 Research and content Cited search, market research, papers, slide decks, MP4 videos, images, local voice, PDF/HWP to Markdown /video , /convert 
 One folder, 14 runtimes One portable .agents/ directory, written into each runtime's own config files oma link cursor 

 Install · First 5 minutes · The team · Which workflow? · Everything in the box · Works with · FAQ · Docs 

 Installation details

The script installs bun if it is missing, installs the oma command globally ( bun install --global oh-my-agent , skipped when oma is already on your PATH), then starts the interactive setup. The hooks (keyword detection and the Stop gate) and several workflows call the globally installed oma command. The hooks silently do nothing if they cannot find it. If you skip the script, install it yourself with bun install --global oh-my-agent ( npm install --global oh-my-agent or brew install oh-my-agent also work).

 
 Windows, or without the install script 

 

 

On Windows the installer hides Antigravity, Hermes, and Kimi, and the hook wrapper is a bash script. The default Aside browser MCP installs through bash , so deselect it if you have no bash.

 

The setup keeps your saved response language or detects it from the system. It asks which agent runtimes to wire up, capability providers, a browser MCP, a model preset, and a skill preset. Choose All for the skill references used across every workflow : domain presets omit some of those skills. Provider availability and task verification remain separate checks.

Choose a preset explicitly when you want a domain's skills:

 

This selects the eight frontend-preset skills. The installer still configures the runtime, providers, and shared workflow files, and retains previously installed skills. Custom selection is available in the interactive installer. See preset values and workflow dependencies.

 
 What the installer also does by default 

- Installs bun (required). Tries uv , Serena ( uv tool install ), and CUE ( brew install cue or winget ), and continues with a warning if any of them fails.
- Pre-selects the Aside browser MCP in the interactive setup, and installs it with curl -fsSL bash only if you keep it selected. Deselect it in the browser MCP step, or change it later with oma update mcp .
- Uses AgentMemory for semantic memory, which runs bun install -g @agentmemory/agentmemory and registers it as a login service (launchd, systemd user unit, or Windows scheduled task). Choose provider none or set OMA NO AGENTMEMORY=1 to skip it.
- Asks before linking skills into home-directory vendor folders (Antigravity, Hermes, Kimi). In $HOME without --global it asks for confirmation.
- Writes some files outside the project without asking: /.claude.json (marks the project as a trusted Claude Code workspace), /.serena/ (OMA context, answer-size floor, project registration), /.cursor/cli-config.json (turns off Cursor's commit attribution), /.grok/config.toml (telemetry), and /.gemini/antigravity-cli/ (HUD), each only for a vendor you selected.
- Writes telemetry opt-outs into vendor settings (Claude DISABLE TELEMETRY=1 , which also turns off Claude Code Remote Control; Gemini, Qwen, Codex, and Grok usage stats). Set telemetry: true to keep vendor defaults.
- Disables Qwen Cod
